bib.title: Python Language Basics, IPython, and Jupyter Notebooks (Chapter 2, Python for Data Analysis, 2nd ed.)

question: What Python language features and IPython/Jupyter tooling does a reader need to follow data-analysis code in the rest of the book?
hypothesis: It is not necessary to become proficient at building good software in Python to productively do data analysis.
contributions: Intro to the Python interpreter, IPython shell and Jupyter notebook
Overview of language semantics, scalar types and control flow

results.quote: float Double-precision (64-bit) floating-point number (note there is no separate double type)

results.claim: Python int has arbitrary precision: 17239871 ** 6 prints exactly.

limits: Deliberately partial: classes and OOP are not covered, and the reader is pointed to the Python tutorial, Python Cookbook, Fluent Python, Effective Python.

Dated: Python 3.6.0, IPython 5.1.0, Jupyter NotebookApp, Qt4Agg backend, %timeit 'best of 3' output; modern IPython/JupyterLab differ. Section 2.3 uses str.format only; f-strings (3.6+) are not shown.
Code in the text is printed with a curly apostrophe in print('It's negative') which is a syntax error as printed.
Jupyter keyboard shortcuts and remote deployment are deferred to the Jupyter menus or the internet.
practices: Experiment with examples in the IPython shell or Jupyter notebooks rather than only reading them (intro, p.15-16).
Use four spaces for indentation and replace tabs with spaces (p.31).
Avoid multiple statements on one line with semicolons (p.31).
Avoid side effects and favour immutability; document side effects if a function has them (p.38).
Test for None with is / is not, since only one None instance exists (p.37).
Check iterability by trying iter(obj) in try/except TypeError rather than testing for __iter__ (p.35).
Use isinstance with a tuple of types to accept several input types (p.34).
Use %matplotlib in the IPython shell and %matplotlib inline in Jupyter, otherwise plots do not appear or block the session (p.29-30).
Use ?, ?? and wildcard ? (np.*load*?) for introspection and docs (p.23-24).
Use %run -i to give a script access to the interactive namespace; %paste/%cpaste to run clipboard code (p.25-26).
Prefer the default range iterator over list(range(n)) since memory use stays small (p.49).
Do not over-use ternary expressions when conditions are complex (p.50).
